errors.text: The proposed example, CoCrFeMnNi, is a quinary alloy rather than the target quaternary FeNiCrMn alloy.
The hypothesis substitutes a micrometer-grained bulk specimen and quasi-static testing for the target single-crystal molecular-dynamics model at 10^8–10^10 s^-1.

It places strain-rate-insensitive yielding above 800 K and attributes it to climb or grain-boundary sliding, whereas the target behavior occurs from 10–600 K and is associated with dislocation nucleation and Shockley-partial glide.
It proposes competing nanotwinning or bulk FCC-to-HCP transformation, while the target reports stacking-fault-induced local HCP-like coordination with no twinning or bulk transformation.
The evidence primarily concerns quinary Cantor alloy polycrystals, creep, or nanowires and therefore does not directly support the claimed yield mechanism and boundary conditions.
